edges.description: Deposited organisms on the ocular surface are sensed by conjunctival epithelial innate antimicrobial programs.
Nasopharyngeal respiratory strains can reach the conjunctival surface and elicit purulent conjunctival inflammation.
The same nasopharyngeal strains can reach the middle ear and produce acute otitis media in conjunctivitis-otitis syndrome.
Host epithelial sensing elicits conjunctival inflammation and mucopurulent exudate.
Inflamed conjunctival vessels produce red-eye hyperemia.
Mucopurulent conjunctival exudate drains as purulent eye discharge.

nodes.description: Young children with acute bacterial conjunctivitis frequently have concurrent acute otitis media as conjunctivitis-otitis syndrome.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and bacterial characteristics of acute bacterial conjunctivitis in children in the antibiotic resistance era.
evidence.snippet: Conjunctivitis-otitis syndrome was found in 32% of patients, of whom 82% of cultures yielded H. influenzae.

nodes.description: Bacteria are deposited on the exposed conjunctival mucosal surface.
Conjunctival epithelial cells constitutively express beta-defensin antimicrobial peptides and can increase beta-defensin production after exposure to S. aureus products.

evidence.reference_title: Roles of human beta-defensins in innate immune defense at the ocular surface: arming and alarming corneal and conjunctival epithelial cells.
evidence.snippet: hBD1, -2, -3 and -4 are constitutively expressed in conjunctival epithelial cells and also partly in cornea.

evidence.reference_title: Roles of human beta-defensins in innate immune defense at the ocular surface: arming and alarming corneal and conjunctival epithelial cells.
evidence.snippet: Staphylococcus aureus increases both hBD2 and hBD3 production in corneal and conjunctival epithelial cells.

nodes.description: Conjunctival inflammation reddens the ocular surface.

evidence.reference_title: [Efficacy assessment of azithromycin 1.5% eye drops versus tobramycin 0.3% on clinical signs of purulent bacterial conjunctivitis].
evidence.snippet: Bacterial conjunctivitis is characterized by hyperemia and discharge of one or both eyes.

nodes.description: In young children, respiratory bacterial strains in the nasopharynx can seed both conjunctival and middle-ear sites, producing the conjunctivitis-otitis syndrome.

evidence.snippet: Pulsed field gel electrophoresis analysis of paired H. influenzae isolates from the conjunctival exudate and middle ear fluid of 21 patients showed identical strains in each patient.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic characteristics of Haemophilus influenzae and Streptococcus pneumoniae isolated from children with conjunctivitis-otitis media syndrome.
evidence.snippet: The causative pathogen responsible for acute conjunctivitis will be originated from the nasopharynx.

nodes.description: Acute conjunctival inflammation produces redness, ocular irritation, and purulent discharge.

evidence.reference_title: Etiology and Outcomes of Acute Infectious Conjunctivitis in Children.
evidence.snippet: Purulent discharge was associated with H influenzae (aOR 2.47, 95% CI 1.23, 5.01) and occurred in 92 (77%) cases in which H influenzae was detected

nodes.description: Acute bacterial conjunctivitis can produce mucopurulent or purulent ocular discharge.

evidence.reference_title: Predicting bacterial cause in infectious conjunctivitis: cohort study on informativeness of combinations of signs and symptoms.
evidence.snippet: 184 adults presenting with a red eye and either (muco)purulent discharge or glued eyelid(s), not wearing contact lenses.

evidence.reference_title: Etiology and Outcomes of Acute Infectious Conjunctivitis in Children.
evidence.snippet: Purulent discharge was associated with H influenzae (aOR 2.47, 95% CI 1.23, 5.01) and occurred in 92 (77%) cases in which H influenzae was detected

nodes.description: Topical antibiotics modestly increase clinical recovery and microbiologic cure in acute bacterial conjunctivitis, but high spontaneous recovery makes delayed prescribing an antibiotic-stewardship option for routine primary care cases.

evidence.reference_title: Antibiotics Versus Placebo for Acute Bacterial Conjunctivitis: Findings From a Cochrane Systematic Review.
evidence.snippet: antibiotics may increase clinical recovery by 26% (risk ratio [RR]: 1.26; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.09-1.46) at the end of therapy

evidence.reference_title: A randomised controlled trial of management strategies for acute infective conjunctivitis in general practice.
evidence.snippet: Delayed prescribing of antibiotics is probably the most appropriate strategy for managing acute conjunctivitis in primary care.

evidence.reference_title: [Efficacy assessment of azithromycin 1.5% eye drops versus tobramycin 0.3% on clinical signs of purulent bacterial conjunctivitis].
evidence.snippet: Clinical cure with azithromycin was not inferior to tobramycin at D9: discharge was absent in 96.3% of patients treated with azithromycin and 95.1% with tobramycin.

evidence.reference_title: Efficacy and safety of azithromycin 1.5% eye drops in paediatric population with purulent bacterial conjunctivitis.
evidence.snippet: Azithromycin was superior to tobramycin in clinical cure rate on D3 (47.1% vs 28.7%, p=0.013) and was non-inferior to tobramycin on D7 (89.2% vs 78.2%, respectively).
